content:
Rumors suggest Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year will revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Below are the three most significant feature differences (excluding price) that may influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth highlighting specifically because it is also the most important point.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic design that iPhones have used for years. Their screen sizes and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first-ever foldable model. Its form factor is entirely different, with an outer screen that is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner screen similar to an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Still Holds the Edge

Apple has always packed its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology into the Pro models. This year will continue that tradition.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to offer largely the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not feature a telephoto lens.

Reports suggest the iPhone Ultra will still carry the same main lens, ultra-wide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro, and is expected to see further improvements this year.

Performance: Both Use the A20 Pro Chip, but Material Differences Affect the Experience

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to use the same A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, their performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will retain the same all-aluminum unibody design as the iPhone 17 Pro, and will also feature a vapor chamber cooling system. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance better than its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures during heavy workloads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a sleek titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, but so far only one leaker has made that claim. However, due to the material differences, even though the iPhone Ultra will carry the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, its performance may be slightly inferior under direct sunlight or during intensive operations.
